_comment: The five Trailhead Guides tools, in the shape an OpenAI-compatible chat API wants them (Azure OpenAI, Ollama, and most others accept this array as-is). Paste the whole array as the 'tools' value in your request body, or lift the objects one at a time as the lab asks for them. The descriptions are the model's only manual: they are the difference between an agent that sequences these correctly and one that guesses.

function.name: search_trails
function.description: Search the trail catalog. Returns matching trails with id, name, park, distance, elevation, difficulty, and features. Call this before recommending any trail; trail ids from here are what the other tools expect.

park.description: Park name, for example 'Glacier National Park'. Partial names like 'Glacier' also match.

features.description: Optional feature keywords to filter on, for example ['lake', 'waterfall', 'wildflowers'].

max_difficulty.description: Optional ceiling on difficulty. 'moderate' returns easy and moderate trails.

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the multi-day forecast and advisories for a park. Returns one entry per date with high, low, conditions, chance of precipitation, and wind.

park.description: Park name, for example 'Glacier National Park'.

function.name: get_trail_conditions
function.description: Get the most recent hiker-submitted condition reports for one trail, newest first. Call this for every trail you intend to recommend. Reports are where closures, washouts, and hazards show up; the catalog entry will not mention them.

trail_id.description: A trail id returned by search_trails, for example 'trail-0117'.

function.name: check_campsites
function.description: Check campground availability for a park. Returns each campground with open sites per date, whether it is frontcountry or backcountry, amenities, and notes such as seasonal closures.

park.description: Park name, for example 'Glacier National Park'.

function.name: request_permit
function.description: Submit a backcountry permit request. This files a request on the user's behalf, so call it once, at the end, after the plan is settled and the user has confirmed.

park.description: Park name, for example 'Glacier National Park'.

zone.description: Permit zone, for example 'Lake McDonald / Sperry' or 'Many Glacier'.

group_size.description: Number of people in the group. Zones cap out at 8 in Glacier.
